facts.statement: The genus Eoazhdarcho was named in 2005 by Chinese paleontologists Lü Junchang and Ji Qiang.
facts.quote: Eoazhdarcho is a genus of probable chaoyangopterid pterosaur named in 2005 by Chinese paleontologists Lü Junchang and Ji Qiang.

facts.statement: The only known species of Eoazhdarcho is Eoazhdarcho liaoxiensis.
facts.quote: The type and only known species is Eoazhdarcho liaoxiensis.

facts.statement: Fossils of Eoazhdarcho were found in the Aptian-age Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation in Chaoyang, Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: The fossil was found in the Aptian-age Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Chaoyang, Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: The species name liaoxiensis refers to the ancient region of Liaoxi.
facts.quote: The specific name, liaoxiensis, refers to the ancient region Liaoxi.

facts.statement: Eoazhdarcho had very elongated metacarpals, while its cervical vertebrae and hind limbs were not elongated.
facts.quote: The metacarpals are very elongated but the cervical vertebrae and hind limbs are not.

facts.statement: In 2008, the clade containing Eoazhdarcho was named Chaoyangopteridae, which is the sister group to Azhdarchidae within Azhdarchoidea.
facts.quote: In 2008 that clade was by Lü, Unwin and colleagues named the Chaoyangopteridae — the sister group of the Azhdarchidae within the much larger clade Azhdarchoidea — with Eoazhdarcho as one of the members.

facts.statement: A 2018 analysis by Longrich and colleagues placed Eoazhdarcho as a basal member of the clade Neopterodactyloidea within Neoazhdarchia.
facts.quote: Later, in 2018, a phylogenetic analysis conducted by paleontologist Nicholas Longrich and colleagues had recovered Eoazhdarcho in a different position within the Neoazhdarchia, as a basal member of the clade Neopterodactyloidea.

facts.statement: In 2025, Thomas and McDavid recovered Eoazhdarcho within the newly named subfamily Shenzhoupterinae.
facts.quote: In 2025, Thomas and McDavid recovered Eoazhdarcho as a chaoyangopterid, specifically within their newly named subfamily Shenzhoupterinae.

facts.statement: Eoazhdarcho lived during the Aptian stage, from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
